findings.title: The layout does not reflow on phone or tablet

location.description: the headline in the two-column hero, squeezed to a 181 px column

findings.viewer_experience: A shop owner who opens the page on a phone or tablet sees a broken page before reading a word: the reader must scroll sideways, the headline runs to 7 lines, and the feature text breaks into one- and two-word lines.

current.value: page 789 px wide in a 390 px (phone) and 768 px (tablet) viewport; h1 at 6.8 characters per line over 7 lines

findings.target: page width equal to the viewport width on phone and tablet, with no sideways scroll; hero and feature paragraphs in one column; each navigation item on one line
findings.fix_direction: Below a breakpoint, stack the hero into one column (text, then buttons, then the table at full width). Stack the three feature paragraphs too. Let the navigation collapse or shrink so each item stays on one line.
findings.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow; Bringhurst on line length, 45 to 75 characters

closed_when.check: page_width equals the viewport width in the phone and tablet viewports, and characters_per_line of h1 and section.facts > p is at least 30 in the phone and tablet viewports

findings.title: The rust "Sign in" button looks like the main call to action, not the trial button

location.description: the filled rust Sign in button at top right, next to the pale trial button in the hero

findings.viewer_experience: The eye goes to the action a new visitor cannot use, and the two hero buttons look equal in weight.

current.value: Sign in: white on #8a3b24, weight 500; Start a 30-day trial: #5c544b on #f3eee6, weight 400

findings.target: one high-emphasis filled accent button per view, and it is the trial button
findings.fix_direction: Give the trial button the filled accent treatment, keep "See how it works" outlined, and set "Sign in" back to a text link or an outline.
findings.source: Material Design 3, Buttons; Apple HIG, accent color kept for the main action

closed_when.check: background of a.button.button-primary is the filled accent color and a.nav-signin has no filled saturated background, in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports

findings.title: On widescreen the hero breaks into two separate islands

location.description: the headline block at the left edge, about 770 px away from the table at the right edge

findings.viewer_experience: The eye has to cross the screen to connect the headline with the table that proves it, and the page looks unfinished rather than calm.

current.value: gap of about 770 px between text block (ends about 604 px) and table (starts 1376 px); feature paragraphs at 79 to 81 characters per line

findings.target: hero and feature row held together as one block of capped width, centered in the window; feature paragraphs at 75 characters per line or fewer
findings.fix_direction: Cap the content width so the hero and the feature row stay together as one readable block, centered in the wide window.
findings.source: Arnheim on balance; Ruder on gathered white space; Bringhurst on line length

closed_when.check: in the widescreen viewport the gap between the right edge of h1 and the left edge of the table is well under 770 px, and characters_per_line of section.facts > p:nth-of-type(1) and (2) is 75 or fewer

findings.title: The table headers and the date are too faint to read

location.description: the table headers Title, On shelf, Sold this week and the date Mon 9 June

findings.viewer_experience: The labels that explain the table are hard to read, and low-vision readers lose them.
findings.fix_direction: Darken them to the #5c544b used for the body text.

closed_when.check: contrast of span.preview-date and thead > tr > th in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports is 4.5 or more

findings.title: Three text sizes are only 1 px apart

location.description: body text sizes across the page: 16 px, 15 px and 14 px

findings.viewer_experience: The sizes read as accidents, not as levels.

current.value: 16 px (paragraph under headline, nav), 15 px (feature text, buttons), 14 px (table)

findings.target: two body sizes, with weight or color for any finer difference
findings.fix_direction: Merge them into two sizes, and use weight or color for any finer difference.

closed_when.check: type_sizes in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports shows no two sizes less than 2 px apart

findings.title: The hero splits the page in halves and the feature row in thirds

location.description: the third feature column, which starts at 859 px while the table starts at 736 px

findings.viewer_experience: The page looks placed by eye.

current.value: table starts at 736 px; third feature column starts at 859 px

findings.target: hero and feature row on one column grid
findings.fix_direction: Put both rows on one column grid.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees the table and a feature column share a left edge in the desktop and widescreen viewports

findings.title: The headline's last line is the single word "asks"
findings.viewer_experience: The headline ends on a lone word.

current.value: last line is the single word "asks"

findings.target: a last line that holds a phrase
findings.fix_direction: Change the line breaks, for example with a narrower column or balanced wrapping, so the last line holds a phrase.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees the last line of the headline hold a phrase of more than one word in the desktop and widescreen viewports

findings.title: "Returns tracked." has no verb or subject, and "the format they take" is unclear

location.description: the third feature paragraph, which starts with Returns tracked.

findings.viewer_experience: It is the only lead-in with no verb or subject, and the reader must guess which format is meant.

current.value: "Returns tracked." and "in the format they take"

findings.target: a lead-in with a verb, and a clear meaning for "the format they take"
findings.fix_direction: Restore the verb, for example "Tracks your returns." The format, or the distributors it supports, is a fact only the maker has; the maker must supply it.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees the Returns lead-in carry a verb, and the format line clear or cut, in all four viewports

findings.title: The table promises "Reorder this week" but shows no reorder quantity

location.description: the table heading Reorder this week above columns for copies on shelf and copies sold

findings.viewer_experience: The reader must work out the reorder from the two numbers.

current.value: columns On shelf and Sold this week only

findings.target: a column that shows how many copies to order, if the product suggests a quantity
findings.fix_direction: If the product suggests a quantity, show that column. Whether it does is a fact only the maker has; the maker must supply it.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees either a column for the quantity to reorder, or a heading that matches the two columns shown, in all four viewports

findings.title: The trial button compares the product with nothing

location.description: the Start a 30-day trial button in the hero

findings.viewer_experience: The shop owner is asked to grade the product, but nothing sets it next to how they count stock today.

current.value: no line that names what Shelfmark replaces

findings.target: a line that names what Shelfmark replaces, so the owner can judge the value on their own terms
findings.fix_direction: Add a line that names what Shelfmark replaces. What it replaces is a fact only the maker has; the maker must supply it.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees a line near the trial button that names what Shelfmark replaces, in all four viewports
